note: Made by the steps in TV_PICTURES.md: the chapter is split into sections that each carry one deep meaning ("sections"), 10 picture ideas are written for each, the top two for each picture are made and the better is chosen by eye (2026-11-22). Wide pictures only (1920x1088); the "tall" names are kept for the day tall pictures are switched back on. Each scene starts at the first word of its verse, or at its "from" words inside the verse. The important part of every picture sits in the upper two thirds, clear of the words. God is not pictured, Job is not portrayed as a biblical person but shown through ordinary people of today, and nothing violent is shown.
method: Second method, asked for by Obay on 2026-11-21 after the sentence-by-sentence pictures did not connect: (1) split the chapter into sections that each carry one deep meaning, written as one plain sentence; (2) write 10 different picture ideas for each section; (3) judge them: which shows the deep meaning most truly, then which a watcher understands at once while hearing the words, then which is most engaging; (4) make the top two for each picture slot as real pictures ("candidates") and choose by eye. A section has one or two pictures. What he said went wrong before: he could not tell why some pictures were there, could not connect them to the meaning, and some were too abstract.

sections.meaning: Life feels like hard, unpaid service: like a labourer longing for shade and his wages, Job has been handed months of emptiness and nights of misery.
ideas: A farmworker bent among crop rows under a blazing midday sun straightens up and looks longingly at the shade of one lone tree far off at the field's edge
A line of tired, dusty workers at the end of a long day waits at a hut window for their pay
A road worker in the heat of the day wipes his brow and stares at the sun still high in the sky
A labourer sits panting in the thin strip of shade of a single fence post in a baking field
A man in work clothes sits slumped on an upturned bucket, his lunch pail empty
A builder carries heavy blocks under a white-hot sky, the shade of a building far out of reach
A tired man stares out of a rain-streaked window at the same grey street, day after day
A labourer's cracked, calloused hands held out open and empty at the end of the day
A night watchman alone at a lonely gate post through a long night
A wall calendar with month after month of blank pages (set aside: numbers would show)

sections.meaning: The nights drag on with tossing until dawn, the body breaks down, and the days fly past and run out without hope, like thread running out on a loom.
ideas: Twisted, knotted bed sheets in the grey first light after a night of tossing, nobody in the bed
A man lies awake on his back in the dark, eyes open, the window still black
A man sits on the edge of his bed at night, head in his hands, watching the window for dawn
A bedside table at dawn crowded with a glass of water, medicine bottles and a lamp left on all night
A loom's shuttle flies across the threads while the last of the thread unwinds from a nearly empty bobbin
A spool of thread almost bare, its last few turns running off it
A weaver's hands at a loom stop as the thread runs out in the middle of a row
The lit windows of a train blur past an empty platform at night
Loose threads hang from a half-finished piece of weaving left on the loom
An hourglass with its last grains running out

sections.meaning: Life is only a breath: once a person is gone he is not seen again, like a cloud that thins away, and he never comes back to his house.
ideas: A lone small white cloud thinning away to nothing in a wide blue sky
A breath of mist on a cold window pane, already fading
Smoke from a blown-out candle curling up and vanishing
An empty armchair by a window, a coat still hanging on the hook by the door
A family house at dusk with the porch light on and no one coming up the path
Footprints on a beach being washed away by a wave
A dandelion clock blown apart by the wind
A man's breath clouding in frosty air and drifting away
A front-door key hanging on a hook in a house now standing empty
A cloud's shadow sliding off a sunlit field

sections.meaning: Job will not keep quiet: he pours out his bitterness, feels hemmed in like the raging sea, finds no rest even in his bed, only terror, and begs to be left alone because his days are only a breath.
ideas: A man stands on a wild shore in a storm, head back, crying out into the wind
A huge stone sea wall holding back crashing storm waves
A man jolts awake from a nightmare in a dark bedroom, sitting bolt upright, hand at his chest
A man sits up in bed at night with the lamp on, too afraid to sleep, staring into the dark
A man at a kitchen table at night pouring out his heart to an empty chair
A rumpled empty bed lit by a flash of lightning
A breath of mist on a cold window pane, fading as you look
A thin thread of smoke rising from a candle just blown out
A man turns his face to the wall with one hand raised: leave me alone
A lone man under a single streetlamp calling out into the night

sections.meaning: What is a mere human, that he should be watched and tested so closely, every morning and every moment, with not even a moment let go?
ideas: A small lone man stands on a vast dark stage under a single hard spotlight
A tiny person standing at the bottom of an enormous open sky
A man sits at a bare table under a bright examination lamp
A lone man in a dark field caught in a searchlight beam
A man on display inside a glass box
A seedling in a laboratory pot under a bright lamp, a ruler set beside it
A small boat alone on a vast still sea
A man walking down an empty street, his long shadow always with him
A specimen on a microscope slide under a bright light
A man standing in the open in hard noon sun with no shade anywhere

sections.meaning: Even if he has sinned, why make him a target and a burden, and why not simply forgive him, before he lies down in the dust and is gone when he is looked for?
ideas: A lone archery target stands in an empty field, arrows in it
A man bent double under a huge heavy sack, trudging up a dusty road
A man carrying a great stone on his back along a dusty track
An empty bed neatly made in morning sun, a pair of worn slippers beside it
Footprints in desert dust that simply stop, the wind blowing dust over them
A wave smoothing away the marks in the sand
An open door onto an empty room with morning light and dust in the air
A worn coat hanging alone on a peg in an empty hallway
A hollow in long grass where someone lay, now empty
A heavy pack set down and left by the side of a path

scenes.principle: Life is hard service: like a labourer who pants for the shade and hopes for his pay, Job has been handed months of emptiness.
scenes.shows: A tired farmworker under a blazing midday sun stands among the crop rows and gazes toward the shade of one lone tree far off at the field's edge.
scenes.prompt: On a wide farm field under a blazing white midday sun, a tired farmworker in a sweat-soaked shirt and straw hat stands among long rows of low crops, straightening his aching back, and gazes longingly toward a single shady tree far off at the edge of the field. The heat shimmers over the dry ground. The man and the distant tree are both clearly visible in the upper part of the frame.

scenes.principle: When I lie down I ask when I will rise; the night drags on and I toss until the morning twilight.
scenes.shows: A bed after a sleepless night: sheets twisted and knotted, the pillow fallen to the floor, grey first light at the window.
scenes.prompt: A bed after a long sleepless night: the sheets and blanket are twisted, knotted and thrown about, the pillow crushed and half on the floor. Grey-blue first light of early morning comes in through a window behind the bed. The room is quiet and empty.

scenes.principle: My days are swifter than a weaver's shuttle and run out without hope; my life is only wind.
scenes.shows: A loom's wooden shuttle flies across the threads, blurred with speed, over a half-woven cloth.
scenes.prompt: A close view of a wooden hand loom in a sunlit workshop. A wooden shuttle is caught flying fast across the stretched threads, blurred with speed, and the last few turns of thread are running off its nearly empty bobbin. A half-woven cloth runs across the loom. Warm daylight from a window.

scenes.principle: A cloud thins away and is gone; so one who goes down to the grave does not come back to his house.
scenes.shows: One small white cloud dissolving into a wide blue sky over a green hill.
scenes.prompt: A wide clear blue sky over a quiet green hill. High in the sky floats one small white cloud that is thinning away at its edges, already half dissolved into the blue, about to vanish completely. Bright clear midday light.

scenes.principle: I will not hold back my mouth; I will complain in the bitterness of my soul. Am I the sea, that you set a guard over me?
scenes.shows: A man stands alone on a rocky shore before a raging storm sea, arms out and head back, crying out.
scenes.prompt: On a wild rocky shore under a dark storm sky, a man in plain clothes stands alone facing the raging sea, his head thrown back and his arms out, crying out into the wind. Huge grey waves break and spray behind him. Cold grey stormy light.

scenes.principle: Even my bed brings no comfort: you terrify me with dreams and visions.
scenes.shows: In a dark bedroom a man jolts awake from a nightmare, sitting bolt upright with his hand pressed to his chest.
scenes.prompt: In a dark bedroom at night a man has just jolted awake from a nightmare: he sits bolt upright in bed, eyes wide with fear, one hand pressed to his chest, the blanket thrown off. Cold blue moonlight from the window falls across him.

scenes.principle: Leave me alone, for my days are a breath.
scenes.shows: A thin thread of smoke curls up from a candle that has just been blown out.
scenes.prompt: A candle that has just been blown out stands on a plain wooden table, and a single thin thread of grey smoke rises from its wick, curling and thinning away into the air. Soft daylight from the side, quiet plain background.

scenes.principle: What is a mortal, that you inspect him every morning and test him every moment, and will not look away from him?
scenes.shows: A small lone man stands on a vast dark stage, caught in a single hard spotlight from above with nowhere to hide.
scenes.prompt: A vast dark empty stage in a huge dark theatre. In the middle stands one small ordinary man in plain clothes, alone, caught in a single hard white spotlight shining straight down on him, squinting and with nowhere to hide. Everything around him is darkness.

scenes.principle: Why have you set me as your target, so that I have become a burden to myself?
scenes.shows: A lone archery target stands in an empty field under a grey sky, arrows stuck in it.
scenes.prompt: A single round archery target on a wooden stand stands alone in the middle of an empty grassy field under a flat overcast sky, several arrows stuck in it. Nothing else in the field.

scenes.principle: Why not take away my guilt? For soon I will lie down in the dust; you will look for me, and I will be no more.
scenes.shows: Morning light falls into a small bedroom through a door just opened: the bed is neatly made and empty, worn slippers beside it.
scenes.prompt: A small plain bedroom in soft early morning light: a single bed is neatly made and empty, a pair of worn slippers side by side beside it, and the door stands open as if someone has come looking. Dust floats in the sunlight. The room is empty.
